word:greek-nt:G0026.explanation: Agape means love. It can describe love shown through patience and kindness.

word:greek-nt:G0079.explanation: Adelphē means sister, referring to a female sibling. It can also refer to a Christian woman among those who do the Father’s will.

word:greek-nt:G0123.explanation: Aigialos means a sea-coast, beach, or shore.

word:greek-nt:G0310.explanation: Anaboao means to cry out or raise one's voice.

word:greek-nt:G0365.explanation: Ananeō means to renew or be renewed.

word:greek-nt:G0422.explanation: This word means “unashamed”: free from disgrace, embarrassment, or a reason to hide. It describes someone or something presented without shame or hesitation. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 2 Timothy 2:15. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea remains a confident lack of shame rather than pride or self-importance.

word:greek-nt:G0480.explanation: Antikeimai means to oppose, resist, or withstand.

word:greek-nt:G0589.explanation: Apodēmeō means to go away from home by traveling into another country.

word:greek-nt:G0673.explanation: Apochōrizō means to separate from or part company.

word:greek-nt:G0747.explanation: Archegos means an originator or author. It can also describe a leader.

word:greek-nt:G0804.explanation: Asphalēs means safe or secure. It can also describe something certain or sure.

word:greek-nt:G0893.explanation: This word describes someone who is not a liar—one whose speech is not false or deceptive. It is an adjective, so it characterizes a person or thing by truthfulness rather than naming an action. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Titus 1:2. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording, but its basic sense is straightforward: not lying or deceitful. The supplied meaning is “not a liar.”

word:greek-nt:G0941.explanation: Bastazō means to carry or bear. It can also mean to take something up.

word:greek-nt:G0978.explanation: Bithynia is the name of a region or geographical area mentioned in the Greek New Testament. It functions as a proper name rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The name appears twice in this corpus: once in Acts 16:7 and once in 1 Peter 1:1. Its precise significance in either passage comes from the surrounding verse and context, but the word itself identifies Bithynia as a particular place.

word:greek-nt:G1102.explanation: Gnapheus means a fuller, someone who cleans woolen cloth.

word:greek-nt:G1230.explanation: Diaginomai means for time to pass or elapse.

word:greek-nt:G1245.explanation: This word means “to clear out.” It is a Greek New Testament verb describing the act of removing what is present so that an area or collection is thoroughly emptied or cleaned. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in Matthew 3:12. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic sense remains straightforward: to clear away material completely rather than merely rearrange or inspect it.

word:greek-nt:G1292.explanation: Diastēma means an interval of time. It can also describe a space or distance between things.

word:greek-nt:G1317.explanation: Didaktikos means able to teach, or apt to teach.

word:greek-nt:G1454.explanation: This word means “resurrection”: the rising of a dead person to life again. It names the event or reality of being raised from death, rather than merely describing ordinary waking or recovery. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Matthew 27:53. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning remains resurrection—the return from death to life. [p03:word:greek-nt:G1454:identity] [p03:word:greek-nt:G1454:occurrences]

word:greek-nt:G1506.explanation: Eilikrinēs means pure. It also means sincere.

word:greek-nt:G1559.explanation: Ekdiōkō means to persecute or drive out.

word:greek-nt:G1685.explanation: Emballō means to cast in or throw into.

word:greek-nt:G1748.explanation: Enedreuō means to lie in wait or ambush someone, seeking to trap him.

word:greek-nt:G1771.explanation: Ennoia means a thought or a mental consideration. In this use, it concerns thoughts of the heart that can be discerned.

word:greek-nt:G1850.explanation: Exousiazō means to exercise authority or power over others. It can also describe being brought under the power of something.

word:greek-nt:G1937.explanation: Epithumeō means to long for or strongly desire something. It can describe an earnest desire to eat with others or to see something. It can also mean to covet another person’s possessions or to lust after a woman.

word:greek-nt:G1991.explanation: Epistērizō means to strengthen or make stronger. It can also mean to confirm, describing disciples who are strengthened or confirmed.

word:greek-nt:G2118.explanation: Euthutēs means straightness or uprightness, and can refer to righteousness.

word:greek-nt:G2121.explanation: Eukairos means opportune, timely, or suitable, describing something that comes at a fitting time.

word:greek-nt:G2187.explanation: Ephraim is the name of a city.

word:greek-nt:G2262.explanation: Er is a personal name, referring to a man named Er rather than expressing an action, quality, or general concept. The name occurs once in the Greek New Testament corpus, in Luke 3:28, and is rendered “Er.” Since the surrounding verse text is not included here, the name’s specific role in that passage cannot be described further. Its basic meaning is therefore the identification of the person called Er.

word:greek-nt:G2396.explanation: ἴδε means “look!”; it calls attention to something.

word:greek-nt:G2514.explanation: This word means “cleanness,” describing a condition of being clean and free from impurity. It refers to the quality or state of cleanness rather than to an action of cleaning. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Hebrews 9:13. Its precise force in that verse belongs to the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is the condition of being clean or pure.

word:greek-nt:G2583.explanation: This word means “rule,” referring to a standard, boundary, or measure that determines the proper scope of something. It functions as a noun and is used four times in the Greek New Testament, all in 2 Corinthians and Galatians. In these passages, it describes the rule or measure by which work and conduct are assessed, rather than suggesting an unrestricted claim or reach. The exact force in any particular verse depends on its surrounding passage, but the central idea remains a governing standard or established boundary.

word:greek-nt:G2600.explanation: Katabasis means descent—a place that goes down.

word:greek-nt:G2675.explanation: Katartizō means to fit or join things together. It can also mean to prepare something for its destination or use. It can mean to complete or bring something into its proper condition. It may describe restoring someone after a fault.

word:greek-nt:G2709.explanation: “Subterranean” describes what is beneath the earth or located under the ground. This Greek New Testament word points to something associated with the world below the earth, rather than what is above it. It appears once in the Greek New Testament, in Philippians 2:10. Because the surrounding verse text is not included here, its precise reference in that sentence must be understood from context, but its basic meaning is “subterranean” or “under the earth.”

word:greek-nt:G2756.explanation: Kenos means empty. It can also describe something vain or futile. Labor is described as not in vain.

word:greek-nt:G2842.explanation: Koinōnia means fellowship or sharing together, and it can describe participation in service to the saints.

word:greek-nt:G2895.explanation: Krabattos means a bed or mat.

word:greek-nt:G2943.explanation: Kyklothen means around or round about.

word:greek-nt:G3034.explanation: Lithazō means to stone or pelt someone with stones.

word:greek-nt:G3377.explanation: Mēnyō means to disclose or inform—to make something known.

word:greek-nt:G3463.explanation: Myrios means ten thousand. It is used with ten thousand talents and ten thousand instructors.

word:greek-nt:G3539.explanation: Noeo means to understand or apprehend—to grasp meaning. It can describe understanding with the heart, in contrast with merely seeing with the eyes.

word:greek-nt:G3661.explanation: Homothumadon means with one mind, unanimously, or in one accord.

word:greek-nt:G3764.explanation: This word expresses that something has never happened or has not happened yet. It is a negative expression that can point either to the complete absence of an event up to that time or to its nonoccurrence so far. The surrounding sentence determines which emphasis is intended. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs four times, so it is relatively uncommon but carries a clear, focused meaning wherever it appears.

word:greek-nt:G3816.explanation: Pais means a child or boy. It can also mean a servant.

word:greek-nt:G3849.explanation: Paraboleuomai means to urge, press, or constrain by entreaties.

word:greek-nt:G3935.explanation: Pariēmi means to let pass or neglect; it can also mean to slacken or loosen.

word:greek-nt:G3940.explanation: Paroikia means sojourning or dwelling as a stranger in a strange land.

word:greek-nt:G4039.explanation: This word describes living around other people or dwelling in a neighborhood. It refers to residence among nearby inhabitants, emphasizing a person’s place within a surrounding community rather than simply being present somewhere. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, at Luke 1:65. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding context, but its basic meaning is residence among those living in the same area.

word:greek-nt:G4066.explanation: Perichōros means neighboring or surrounding and can describe a region around a place.

word:greek-nt:G4163.explanation: Poiētēs can refer to a poet. It can also mean a doer, someone who carries out what is heard rather than merely hearing it.

word:greek-nt:G4264.explanation: Probibazo means to prompt or urge someone.

word:greek-nt:G4358.explanation: Prosormizo means to anchor at a place, or to moor.

word:greek-nt:G4534.explanation: This Greek New Testament word is the name “Salmone.” It functions as a proper name rather than a general description or action, identifying a particular named subject in the text. It occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at Acts 27:7, and is rendered “Salmone” in the available English translations. The precise referent of the name is determined by the surrounding verse and passage.

word:greek-nt:G4732.explanation: Stereō means to strengthen or make strong. It can also mean to establish something.

word:greek-nt:G4790.explanation: This Greek New Testament word means “to share with,” describing participation or partnership with someone else. It expresses joining another person in what they are doing, experiencing, or receiving, rather than remaining separate from it. The word occurs three times in the Greek New Testament, in Ephesians, Philippians, and Revelation. Its precise emphasis in each verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea remains active participation with others. It can therefore describe sharing in a matter, associating with it, or taking part alongside someone.

word:greek-nt:G4831.explanation: This word describes a fellow imitator—someone who imitates along with another person or group. It presents imitation as a shared activity rather than something done alone. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, so its precise force in Philippians 3:17 depends on the surrounding verse and passage. Its central idea remains clear: joining others in following the same example or pattern.

word:greek-nt:G4897.explanation: This word means “to enter together with” or “to enter with.” It describes the action of going into a place alongside another person or group, emphasizing shared entry rather than merely being inside. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both times in John, where the surrounding wording determines who enters with whom. Its basic sense is straightforward: accompanying someone as they go in. This is an action word, so it describes movement into a place in company with others.

word:greek-nt:G4912.explanation: Synechō means to press, hold fast, or confine. It can also describe being afflicted with sickness, as with a great fever.

word:greek-nt:G5160.explanation: Trophē means food or nourishment. It can also refer to provisions supplied for people.

word:greek-nt:G5241.explanation: This word means “intercedes” or “to intercede.” It describes intervening on behalf of another person, especially by presenting an appeal or request for them. As a verb, it expresses an action performed for someone else rather than a mere feeling or concern. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Romans 8:26. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea is interceding on another’s behalf.

word:greek-nt:G5278.explanation: Hypomenō means to endure or bear up under trouble. It can also mean to remain behind or stay in a place.

word:greek-nt:G5304.explanation: Hysteresis means poverty, want, or need.

word:greek-nt:G5393.explanation: Phlegon is a Roman Christian man.

word:greek-nt:G5472.explanation: Chalcedony means a small stone of various colors.

word:greek-nt:G5511.explanation: Chlamys means a short cloak, or robe. It describes clothing that can be put on and taken off.

word:greek-nt:G5528.explanation: Chortos means grass. It can also mean hay.

word:greek-nt:G6055.explanation: κλιναρίων means a cot or bed.
